source: User clarification: only Train and Test; both labeled during Meaning Loop; Test never participates in guideline generation; Train errors drive expression development.

updates.title: An end-to-end agent system
updates.prompt: Create one finished 16:9 research slide. Match the referenced illustrated deck: white background, navy bold readable text, small orange robots, teal human decisions, purple document evidence, blue model tools, pastel local panels, generous spacing, no enclosing slide frame. All wording English. This is proposed workflow, not measured results. No fake numbers. Keep model weights fixed. Preserve page number specified. Every arrow must have a clear source and destination; do not draw a held-out example/error flowing into guideline development. Redesign this overview so the data split is visible. Keep title "An end-to-end agent system". Subtitle "Train develops the guideline. Held-out data checks execution." Use a clean horizontal main row with FOUR connected stations: '0  Itemize + split' → '1  Frame task' → a large teal 'MEANING LOOP · 2–4' with substeps 'Explore / Human forms / Integrate' → a large purple 'EXPRESSION LOOP · 5' with 'Rewrite / Execute / Compare'. Clearly label a purple document strip under both loops 'TRAIN / LEARNING' and short caption 'Cases and errors can refine the guideline', with arrows from Train strip upward into BOTH loops. Between loops show two small paired output icons 'Approved meaning' and 'Train reference labels'. A short blue return connector inside Expression indicates repeated wording trials. A teal return from Expression back to Meaning labeled 'Unresolved meaning'. Under Expression a separate blue locked box 'VALIDATION' / 'Aggregate feedback for selection', arrow to Expression's Compare station ONLY. On far right below main row a locked '6  Freeze + FINAL TEST' / 'Independent assessment' then an arrow down or right to '7  Large-scale labeling + audit'. TEST must have no arrow back into either development loop. Draw a visually distinct line from selected Expression candidate to Step6. Footer 'Train, validation and test receive labels. Their roles and visibility differ.' Page6. Keep fewer than140 words and clearly readable; small friendly robot at loop headings, no oversized decorative figures.
updates.notes: Version 10 explicitly names Train (learning), Validation and Final Test in the overview. Step0 groups related items and reserves partitions before exploration; Step1 frames the task. Train content, judgments and errors can develop meaning and expression. Only allowed validation aggregates guide selection. Final-test content and reference labels remain in separate custody and are used after the candidate and protocol are frozen. Executors label assigned held-out items in separate contexts, so held-out data is labeled without becoming guideline-development evidence. Meaning and Train reference labels enter Expression as separate versioned artifacts, with reference answers hidden from executor prompts. Semantic escalation returns to Meaning. Weights remain fixed; Train describes guideline-development data, not neural training.
updates.revisionPrompt: Keep the main top workflow and two partitions, improve the missing connections. In Step4 replace "Apply and check on train cases." with "Integrate Train judgments." Add a compact badge on the arrow between Meaning and Expression reading "Guideline + Train reference labels". Add an orange rightward arrow from Expression panel to Step6 labelled "Freeze candidate". In the empty lower half add a teal return arrow from Expression to Meaning labelled "Unresolved meaning". Below this add a separate simple horizontal application route: "Current guideline" → "Label Train + Test" → "Versioned reference labels". Label this route "During Meaning Loop: apply rules, do not change them from Test". No arrow from this route back to rule development. Reference-label icon visible. Keep Train strip only feeds development. Footer unchanged, page6. Do not put step7 inside the Test panel: keep step7 at far right lower as separate scale/audit activity. No Validation anywhere.

updates.title: Step 0: transform the corpus into items
updates.prompt: Create one finished 16:9 research slide. Match the referenced illustrated deck: white background, navy bold readable text, small orange robots, teal human decisions, purple document evidence, blue model tools, pastel local panels, generous spacing, no enclosing slide frame. All wording English. This is proposed workflow, not measured results. No fake numbers. Keep model weights fixed. Preserve page number specified. Every arrow must have a clear source and destination; do not draw a held-out example/error flowing into guideline development. Edit this Step0 slide. Preserve the title, subtitle, main raw-corpus → itemization-agent → annotation-items row, item fields, and the middle conversation/context example. Redesign only the bottom row to make THREE explicit split outputs large and readable. Bottom left shorter teal 'CHECK ITEMS' box with 'IDs · Context · Duplicates · Source groups'. To its right a branch labeled 'Keep related items together' ends in THREE vertically stacked document cards: purple 'TRAIN / LEARNING' / 'Guideline development'; blue locked 'VALIDATION' / 'Candidate selection'; dark navy locked 'FINAL TEST' / 'Independent assessment'. Do not keep the old generic Development items / Held-out items labels. Slightly reduce middle-row height if needed so the bottom three cards and text are readable. Footer 'Split before exploration. All three sets can receive labels.' Page7. No percentage or item count, no model weight training.
updates.notes: Step0 now makes partitions explicit after stable item/context/source grouping and before exploration, retrieval or embedding for development. Related conversations and near-duplicate groups stay together. Train is the learning pool for guideline development; validation is repeatedly used for allowed aggregate candidate selection; final test is reserved for independent assessment. No fixed split ratio is prescribed. All partitions may receive predictions and separately reviewed reference labels, but their storage, tool contexts and disclosure permissions differ. Exposed historical data cannot become pristine test merely by renaming it. Model weights remain fixed.

updates.title: Step 5: improve expression without changing meaning
updates.prompt: Create one finished 16:9 research slide. Match the referenced illustrated deck: white background, navy bold readable text, small orange robots, teal human decisions, purple document evidence, blue model tools, pastel local panels, generous spacing, no enclosing slide frame. All wording English. This is proposed workflow, not measured results. No fake numbers. Keep model weights fixed. Preserve page number specified. Every arrow must have a clear source and destination; do not draw a held-out example/error flowing into guideline development. Redesign this slide preserving the title "Step 5: improve expression without changing meaning". Subtitle "Train errors guide rewriting. Validation summaries guide selection." At top teal lock 'APPROVED MEANING STAYS FIXED'. LEFT 60% large purple/turquoise loop with three large stations: orange robot 'REWRITE GUIDELINE', blue chips 'LABEL TRAIN ITEMS', scoring/magnifier 'INSPECT TRAIN ERRORS'. Clockwise arrows close this loop. Near Train scoring a separate document 'APPROVED TRAIN LABELS' with arrow ONLY into scoring, caption 'Hidden from executors'. Label loop 'TRAIN / LEARNING'. RIGHT40% separate pale-blue panel 'VALIDATION' containing vertical sequence 'Candidate guideline + validation items' → 'Separate executor + scorer' → 'Quality / coverage / speed summaries'. Small separate locked reference icon feeds scorer ONLY labeled 'Validation references'. A dashed arrow FROM the summary bottom to a 'SELECT CANDIDATE' small box between panels labeled 'Aggregates only'; selected candidate can inform next rewrite, no raw validation case arrow. Below the Train loop a short teal callout 'Meaning gap? Send an issue to the Meaning Agent'. Bottom dark navy lock banner 'FINAL TEST STAYS CLOSED UNTIL STEP 6'. Footer 'Train is for guideline development. No model weights change.' Page12. Keep readable and avoid overlapping arrows; no numeric metrics.
updates.notes: The Expression Loop uses Train content and item-level errors for rewriting. Executors receive the guideline and permitted input context, never reference answers. Dedicated validation execution/scoring services return only an allowlisted aggregate view to the developer. Full validation content, predictions, per-item errors and references remain outside developer-visible storage and conversations. Aggregate selection is repeated evaluation and can overfit; use a declared query budget and separate final test. Quality, coverage and stronger-model regression constraints precede gap reduction. A semantic issue routes through the Meaning Agent. Train does not imply model-weight updates.
updates.revisionPrompt: Edit only three details. Add a teal lock badge near the top of Train panel reading "APPROVED MEANING STAYS FIXED". Change "Small meaning gap?" to "Meaning issue?". Add one clear rightward arrow from FREEZE SELECTED CANDIDATE box to the TEST panel. No arrow from Test back to development. Keep all other content exactly unchanged, page12.

updates.title: Step 6: assess the frozen candidate on final test
updates.prompt: Create one finished 16:9 research slide. Match the referenced illustrated deck: white background, navy bold readable text, small orange robots, teal human decisions, purple document evidence, blue model tools, pastel local panels, generous spacing, no enclosing slide frame. All wording English. This is proposed workflow, not measured results. No fake numbers. Keep model weights fixed. Preserve page number specified. Every arrow must have a clear source and destination; do not draw a held-out example/error flowing into guideline development. Redesign this slide to remove model-selection-on-test ambiguity. Title "Step 6: assess the frozen candidate on final test". Subtitle "Select on validation first. Use test for independent assessment." Main row left teal locked file 'FROZEN CANDIDATE' / 'Meaning + expression + executor settings', center blue chips 'TEST EXECUTOR' / 'Guideline + test items', right blue chart 'INDEPENDENT SCORER' / 'Quality · Coverage · Speed'. Arrows left→center→right. Below center add a separate large navy locked stack 'FINAL TEST ITEMS' arrow upward ONLY to Test Executor. Below scorer add teal human/document stack 'HUMAN-REVIEWED TEST REFERENCES' arrow upward ONLY to scorer. Clearly label 'Reference answers hidden from executor'. Bottom two alternative outcome boxes from scorer 'PASS: release the frozen candidate' and 'FAIL: hold release'. NO arrow from test back into guideline rewriting or Meaning. Footer 'If test findings guide changes, use a fresh independent test for the next claim.' Page13. No measured scores or selected green status. Test reference judgments are frozen before predictions, captured in notes; avoid tiny paragraphs.
updates.notes: Candidate and executor selection occurs using development/validation, not final-test performance. Freeze meaning, expression, output schema, model/runtime configuration, reference release, metric definitions and thresholds before final-test execution. Independent human test references are adjudicated and locked before viewing candidate predictions. Executors see assigned test items but not reference answers. A dedicated scorer joins predictions to references and reports prespecified metrics. Failure holds release rather than automatically retuning against test cases. If inspected test findings influence changes, that set is no longer fresh final evidence and a new independent test is required for the next claim. All workflow states are proposals, not experiment outcomes.

updates.title: The experiment view separates Train, Validation and Test
updates.prompt: Redesign this Workbench UI slide while preserving its white/navy/teal/purple/blue palette, small orange robot, same top app navigation and page19. Title "Train, validation and test have different roles". Subtitle "The experiment view makes each data boundary visible". Top app bar "Labeling Workbench" / "Supportive replies", tabs Data Labeling Quality Delivery with Quality active. Below a teal lock strip 'Approved meaning v2' and blue 'Expression candidate e03'. Main content THREE equal width panels across the screen. LEFT purple panel header 'TRAIN / LEARNING', description 'Develop the guideline', three readable rows 'Inspect cases and errors', 'Rewrite the expression', 'Review affected learning labels', button 'Open learning errors'. MIDDLE blue panel header 'VALIDATION', description 'Select a candidate', a readable two-column table headers 'Measure' and 'Result' with rows 'Quality', 'Coverage', 'Speed', all Result cells a dash; badge 'Not run'; helper 'Summaries only; cases stay protected', button 'Review run settings'. RIGHT navy/gray locked panel header 'FINAL TEST', description 'Assess after freezing', lines 'Items and references protected', 'No guideline development', disabled button 'Available after freeze'. Below all panels a thin orange agent strip 'Meaning issue?' / 'Expression Agent sends an issue to the Meaning Agent'. Footer 'All sets receive labels. Only Train examples enter guideline development.' Additional small line 'Concept UI · No model results yet.' Page19. Do not add fake metrics, selected test results, huge decorative graphics, or hide the words TRAIN VALIDATION TEST.
updates.notes: The UI makes the three datasets first-class rather than hiding them behind a generic model testing page. Train permits developer-facing item-level content and errors. Validation exposes bounded metrics for selection, while its raw inputs, predictions/errors and references remain with separate evaluator/scorer roles. Final test remains closed to developers and is executed only after the selected candidate and protocol are frozen. All sets can receive task labels and diagnostics, but a developer's visibility differs from an executor's. No results are shown; dashes are unrun placeholders. Semantic questions return through the Meaning Agent without leaking protected examples.

updates.title: Meaning Loop labels both Train and Test
updates.prompt:
Create a finished 16:9 conceptual slide in the reference deck style: white, navy text, teal human decisions, purple documents, blue executor chips, small orange robots, no outer border. Title "Meaning Loop labels both Train and Test". Subtitle "Only Train evidence changes the guideline". Page21. Make a very legible workflow with two simple horizontal bands and ample whitespace, not a dense chart.
Upper two-thirds is a pale teal local panel headed "MEANING LOOP" with two clearly separated horizontal lanes:
Lane A "DEVELOP THE GUIDELINE": purple "Train cases" → orange agent with human "Explore · Decide · Refine" → teal document "Guideline vN". A small teal curved return arrow from Guideline vN to Explore labeled "Train feedback". NO test in this lane.
Lane B "APPLY THE GUIDELINE": a short one-way arrow downward from Guideline vN goes to a central "Label under vN" chip. On its left, two separate document inputs "Train items" and "Test items" feed this labeling chip. On its right, the chip branches to TWO clearly separate output cards "Train reference labels" and "Test reference labels". Each says "Human-reviewed · Version vN". Use small icons; do not crowd. A note beside the Test reference output: "No feedback to rule design".
Lower third outside the panel is blue "EXPRESSION LOOP": "Train errors" → "Rewrite expression" with a curved loop back indicating iteration. Small lock "Meaning stays fixed". Then one rightward arrow "Freeze" → navy "Test assessment". Feed the Train reference labels output to Train errors with a thin blue arrow; feed Test reference labels output ONLY into Test assessment with a thin navy arrow. No Test-to-rewrite arrow.
Footer "If Train changes the rules, recheck affected labels in both sets. Model weights stay fixed."
All labels English, no validation split. Current meaning may evolve in Meaning Loop; only the final performance evaluation waits for freezing. Human-reviewed reference labels are distinct from executor predictions. This is a proposed design, no scores.
updates.notes: This companion slide addresses the user's core distinction: Train, Validation and Test are all labelable. Train supports source/case exploration, human preference elicitation, rule development and expression debugging. Dedicated evaluators apply the candidate/frozen guideline to held-out inputs, while human reference adjudication and scoring happen in separate custody. Reference answers are hidden from executors; raw held-out examples and item-level errors are hidden from developers. Validation aggregates can influence candidate selection, which is why a separate final test is needed. Final test receives labels and independent evaluation after freezing, with no development return arrow. The guideline's meaning is shared, but candidate vs frozen expression timing differs. Train means guideline development; this system does not train model weights.
